neighbours.label: the '-ie' diminutive ending of a first name (Stevie, Frankie, Richie, Robbie)
fire: We spent the evening listening to old records by Stevie Wonder.
My uncle Frankie used to play guitar in a pub band.
The coach told Robbie to warm up before the second half.
At the party, Freddie sang three songs in a row.
Her best friend Jonnie moved to Glasgow last year.
The comedian Richie told the same joke twice.
On the poster, Lizzie and Maggie stood side by side.
The kids waited for Charlie to bring the ball.
quiet: We spent the evening listening to old records by Steve Miller.
My uncle Frank used to play guitar in a pub band.
The coach told Robert to warm up before the second half.
At the party, Fred sang three songs in a row.
Her best friend John moved to Glasgow last year.
The comedian Richard told the same joke twice.
On the poster, Elizabeth and Margaret stood side by side.
The kids waited for Charles to bring the ball.

notes: card: 'Ste|vie', 'Frank|ie', 'Jon|nie', ' Richie', ' Robbie', ' Freddie'; + pole is the 'doggie/doggy' diminutive
